title: Claude formalizes Fermat's theorem in Lean
summary: A proof of Fermat's Last Theorem fully machine-verified in Lean: Claude produced most of it independently over 11 days, with about 13 million lines and 29,500 intermediate theorems, and a comparator confirms that its statement matches Mathlib's. It follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof, uses Mathlib and parts of an Imperial College project, and is probably longer than necessary.

evidence.tested: The proof was checked by Lean using only standard axioms; a comparator tool confirmed the theorem statement matches Mathlib's, and mathematician Kevin Buzzard reviewed it.
evidence.unknown: The proof is about 13 million lines and likely much longer than needed; it follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof and is presented as verification, not new mathematics.
evidence.ai_role: Dozens of agents worked for 11 days on the Prove2Me platform, producing about 30,300 computer-verified theorems; humans gave occasional high-level instructions.
